learning_curve_arm.why: the uploaded paper (Advanced Computational Frameworks for Vertebral Body Detection and 2D/3D Registration in Intraoperative Fluoroscopy, section 2): a ~90 % plateau in fluoroscopy is sampling-density saturation of the acquisition space, not model capacity; accuracy should be read against sample count and against acquisition-space coverage (bins per dimension, normalised entropy H* = -sum p log p / log K), and the lever is the sparse bins, not more of the same data. The paper says nothing about the optimiser's learning rate.
learning_curve_arm.what: the D1 recipe, unchanged, fitted on nested, person-grouped, subtype-stratified fractions of the training persons (permutation prefix at --fraction-seed = seed), seeds 0-2; the three D1 heads are the top of the curve. NOT D1: no tau written, registry stage recurrent_head_dual_lcurve, train_list recorded as the whole #train (a superset, conservative for the leak gate) with the kept persons and their sha256 in each dual json and in the registry params

T13.note: 0.00 at 1.0 on every seed (79 crops of the one T13 validation person); the small fractions name a few by chance

learning_curve_arm.reading: real-film naming is saturated in sample count (98.2 -> 98.7 % over a 16-fold increase in training persons; the last doubling gained 0.10 points, inside the 0.16-point seed spread). Render naming, the fluoro-like poses, climbs about one point per doubling and has not stopped (band 9: +1.09 points on the last doubling against a 0.65-point spread); at that rate another 16-fold of the same data would buy about four points, not the 30-point gap to the films. The saturation rule here is a description (last doubling's gain <= the seed spread at 1.0), not a test.
